Ruling: stay on main and commit exact owned paths. This follows the user's
established active-branch preference and preserves the running consumer. The cost
is that all reviews must isolate our commits from other chats' commits.

Ruling: execute the long plan through subagent-driven-development, one implementer
at a time and independent review gates. This replaces the initial inline workflow.
Cost if wrong: additional handoff latency and context reconstruction; task reports
and isolated review packages preserve the evidence for correction.

Ruling: preserve externally initialized caller depth and explicitly reject an
incompatible retained-graph resize in that specialized path. Normal clear-depth
resize uses bounded same-encoder scaling and continues staging. Silently replacing
caller depth breaks compositing; the cost is that callers combining loaded
external depth, graph resize and staged replacement must supply a compatible
graph/depth contract. Require failed-admission cleanup and successful retry tests.

Ruling: use a focused generic PublicationGroup child-publication boundary for
tile cover staging, with separate candidate render and displayed pick traversal.
This avoids Earth types in core and per-frame BVH capture. It must preserve
retained instances or frozen pick properties through styling/visibility changes,
match the exact submitted candidate receipt, and update all render capability
traversals. The contract does not claim arbitrary whole-scene mutation snapshots.
Cost if wrong: revise this public group API and its traversal integrations before
dependent consumers ship. Concrete retained-cover style mutation risk sent to
worker for validation before finalizing the mechanism.

Ruling: retained published submissions conservatively enable color visibility
for their already-included meshes while camera reprojection is active. Authored
visibility/layer inclusion and saved clipping remain unchanged; current GPU
clipping handles offscreen content. This prevents old frustum flags hiding a
newly visible retained mesh during staging. Cost if wrong: extra transient draws
until publication, or revisit retained bounds culling. Regression verifies native
pixels, frozen picks and ordinary culling restored after publication.

Ruling: split Task8 into sequential8a transmission,8b local probes and8c SSR/AO,
each with its own implementation and independent review gate. All original scope
remains required. These are separate resource/publication contracts large enough
to benefit from focused review. Cost if wrong: additional handoffs and integration
rework, checked by Task9 whole-change review. Derived task-8a/b/c-brief files
preserve the complete original Task8 requirements as context.

Ruling: replace fixed-side cloud ping-pong graphs with stable scratch resolve
and publish into output plus persistent history. Keep and prepare the actually
displayed cloud candidate while a new candidate stages; advance only executed
history, including the same candidate during incomplete tile admission. This
resolves retained graph versus mutable uniform/CPU-side disagreement. Share
shadow/lighting assets only with explicit ownership and bounded old/new admission.
Cost if wrong: extra history-copy bandwidth and candidate overlap memory, or
rework this history contract; native prolonged staging/resize/failure tests required.

Ruling: shadow temporal CPU matrices track successful ordered shadow graph
execution independently of main-scene presentation. Task2 graph completion is
queued, so this records submitted resource history, not physical presentation.
Terminal failure must invalidate it. Cost if wrong: stale shadow reprojection
after failure/cadence skips; verify graph/matrix identity and recovery tests.

Ruling: use explicitly scoped scene-frame GPU pressure for opt-in cloud adaptation,
with bounded discrete ray-resolution and cadence levels, stable requested presets
and null/partial samples inert. Current backend cannot measure individual cloud
passes. Cost if wrong: non-cloud scene load can reduce cloud quality without
solving the bottleneck; expose effective settings and validate useful response.

Ruling: adaptive ray work uses a bounded active grid inside retained maximum raw
target allocation, with fixed resolve/history targets. Validate each stride's
phase coverage/convergence and avoid rays outside the active grid. Cost if wrong:
maximum allocation remains resident and coarser sampling can reduce detail;
native motion/grain evidence must expose that tradeoff, not claim memory savings.

Ruling: shadow cadence may skip only with stable valid cascade maps and unchanged
density/lighting state. Independent weather/shape/detail velocities and radial
evolution force updates because no exact single advection exists. Keep sampled
matrices tied to computed maps. Cost if wrong: limited cadence savings with
animated weather; prevents incorrect sliding/stale shadows at the cost of work.

Ruling: keep cloud requested candidate separate from the bound candidate, install
bindings only during serialized frame preparation, and retain immutable candidate
and history submission records until receipt or proven failed publication. Retire
only outside active/bound/displayed/submission ownership. Reason: setters can run
while later hooks or the backend await. Cost if wrong: extra held candidates consume
the existing cap and can reject quality changes; ownership mistakes freeze the
visible graph or prematurely free native resources.

Ruling: after a successful backend receipt, notify every attached afterRender
plugin even if an earlier hook throws, then rethrow the first original error and
stack after staging invalidation. Reason: native publication has already occurred,
so every displayed-state owner must observe it. Cost if wrong: hooks that formerly
never ran after another hook failure will now run; preserve caller error and cover
that lifecycle explicitly with a core test and a native cloud regression.

Ruling: add prepared replacement tokens to AtmosphereCloudRegistration. Cloud
setters prepare and retain complete atmosphere composition before accepting new
settings; serialized frame preparation publishes without new GPU allocation.
Retired unbound requests close their tokens. Atmosphere source/LUT/aerial/viewport
changes transactionally rebuild outstanding tokens before committing state,
rolling back all newly prepared resources on failure. Reason: preserve both
setter allocation atomicity and in-flight registration identity. Cost if wrong:
more prepared ownership, tighter atmosphere/cloud mutation coupling and transient
old/new overlap can reject changes sooner under existing caps; stale token
publication would require rework and could display mismatched atmosphere inputs.
Worker owns atmosphere/plugin.dart and focused token/rebuild failure tests forfix2.

Ruling: expose generic PluginContext.isPreparingFrame(FrameInfo), backed by an
engine/frame-specific beforeRender zone marker invalidated in finally. Token
publication checks it inside its serialized action. Reason: enforce publication
phase while allowing a later dependent plugin hook to bind prepared composition;
inPluginHook alone also accepts attach/afterRender. Cost if wrong: small public
lifecycle API and zone bookkeeping; incorrect marker lifetime could admit escaped
asynchronous binding mutation. Verify exactengine/frameidentity, delayedqueue,
backendawait, afterRender,attachandescapedunawaitedcallback rejection. No renderer
change. Fix2ownership includes minimal engine/context predicate and focusedtests.

Ruling: retain nonzero-cloud large-motion sky/haze evidence and isolate rectangular
atmosphere resize with zero cloud density, maintaining nontrivial sky/haze and
motion. Reason: different cloud sampling grids are not equal-content references.
No tolerance change; preserve the failed attempt and dimensions. Cost if wrong:
this comparison cannot establish exact nonzero-cloud rectangular-resize behavior.
Worker may add same-aspect equal-grid coverage if it directly addresses that facet.

Ruling: Task6 uses conservative built-in opaque triangle eligibility, ordering
barriers and disjoint transformed-bounds checks for ambiguous overlaps/ties,
with bounded lookahead for pipeline/material/coarse-depth grouping. Batch only
consecutive compatible ordinary meshes, preserving original packet identities.
Explicit instances, deformation/custom shaders, transmission, outline, partial
coverage and native temporal-AA frames retain supported unbatched paths. Cloud
temporal reconstruction alone does not trigger the native temporal-AA exclusion.
Reason: avoid pixel-order, picking and history changes while reducing compatible
work. Cost if wrong: fewer batching gains in overlapping/complex/temporal scenes;
possible missed performance, not permission to alter output. Internal batch-cache
resources must be separately capped, fully preflighted/serial-retired and safely
fall back when optimization memory cannot fit, without raising existing caps.
Worker proceeds to immediate-before baseline and implementation; report selected
bounds and actual native counter propagation.

Ruling: Task6 optional batch cache uses one renderer-owned buffer capped at4MiB,
256batches and64-draw reorder windows. ResourceStore records only its ResourceKey
and preparation pin, with CPU recipe data in renderer and no persistent GPU aliases.
On required allocation failure, use complete-request registry credit (including
existing planned releases) before retiring only unique completed optional ownership.
Rejected requests that still cannot fit retain the cache. Prepare batches after
required scene allocations, pin through encoding/submission, unpin on completion
and every abort. Apply the same private reclaim to validated public registry
allocations between frames, before the next native begin_profile. Reason: optional
acceleration must not block otherwise-fitting required scene/cloud/graph resources.
Cost if wrong: extra preflight bookkeeping and cache rebuilds under memory pressure;
an incorrect pin or hidden GPU alias would violate accounting/lifetime. Require
inter-frame public allocation, preparation-pin and rejection-preservation tests.
No public IDs, generic callback API, raised budget or forced per-frame reupload.

Ruling: constrain only the NdotV=0 LUT endpoint to the analytic correlated-Smith
white grazing limit Ewhite=1 by finite, nonzero normalization of A/B, preserving
the sampled Schlick channel ratio. Leave non-endpoint NDF samples unchanged.
Reason: G2/G1v tends1 as LambdaV tends infinity and visible-normal reflections
remain above the surface except measure-zero boundaries; independent VNDF gives
A+B approximately1. This removes a known endpoint quadrature bias at constant
cost while keeping independent reference sampling. Cost if wrong: the estimated
colored Fresnel split and adjacent grazing samples remain approximate; test both
channels, roughness0 and adjacent/low-NdotV columns without loosening tolerance.

Ruling: preserve the mixed-owner68e4744f history and concurrent ML content, isolate
its rendering paths in evidence/review, and require a temporary index for every
subsequent commit. Reason: rewriting shared main would disturb other active work;
exact staging on the shared index proved insufficient under concurrent commits.
Cost if wrong: this commit remains non-atomic across owners, review needs a path
filter, and future commit/index reconciliation takes extra care.

Ruling: retain conservative PBR view/pending ownership and warm LUT retention,
but defer fallback allocation/generation until a prepared PBR frame actually
needs a fallback BRDF rather than a supplied environment BRDF. Reason: supplied
BRDF-only scenes should not pay an unused131072-byte allocation, cold integration
pass or budget rejection. Cost if wrong: first switching from a supplied BRDF to
fallback can incur its cold generation cost later; environment/staging ordering
must preserve the actually displayed frame and be tested. Worker asked for the
small conditional refinement plus supplied-first, toggle/staged and last-owner
checks, or a concrete ordering constraint before broader architecture changes.

Ruling: pipeline recovery uses separate candidate maps and publishes only after
GPU error scopes succeed across the complete main/outline/transmission request.
Keep the prior useful cache and layout-retirement queue unchanged on failure.
Steady limits remain512pipelines/128physical modules+layouts; preparation can hold
one old cache plus one admitted missing set, bounded1024/256handles, excluding
already encoded wgpu-owned lifetimes. Reason: recoverable retries cannot reuse
invalid handles or lose the last useful cache. Cost if wrong: higher transient
pipeline/layout retention and potential earlier memory-pressure rejection. A real
GPU validation failure after valid candidates, full-cache rollback, retirement
queue invariance and successful retry will test the transaction boundary.

Ruling: reuse opaque capture by seeding main color and depth, then skip only the
matching contiguous opaque prefix in actual sorted order. Require exact formats,
single-sample targets, no loaded external depth, identical clear/background/color/
depth semantics and no intervening consumers or transparency. MSAA and other
incompatible cases retain existing redraw. Reason: save duplicate geometry work
without changing explicit order or composition. Cost if wrong: one fullscreen
seed pass and conservative missed optimization; mismatched eligibility could
change pixels, so native reference images and actual pass work must verify it.

Ruling: smooth transmission may collapse to one depth-aware bilinear tap only
when the actual effective filter radius collapses; rough transmission retains
bounded nine-tap filtering and dispersion keeps its channel paths. Reason: avoid
redundant smooth-glass samples while preserving rejection and fallback. Cost if
wrong: boundary/filter mismatch could alter glass; use the filtered Task7 material
response and native shader work/image comparisons, not an assumed FPS gain.

Ruling: add optional CaptureBackend.createCaptureView() leases, rendering a
FrameSubmission into a validated same-device RGBA16F texture through the shared
GPU protocol. Keep sealed OutputTarget and OS channels unchanged. Each lease has
independent view/admission/history identity and shared immutable geometry, with
linear HDR output and no recursive main-engine hooks. Reason: probes need actual
GPU capture on presenter-owned devices. Cost if wrong: a new public capability,
protocol and resource-lifetime surface; cross-view ownership mistakes could leak
or corrupt targets, so native lifecycle and device-generation checks are required.

Ruling: auxiliary captures return after ordered queue submission rather than the
surface/readback completion fence. Accept auxiliary admission/history at that
submission boundary, retain resources until genuinely completed serials, and use
existing queue backpressure. Keep ordinary presenter/readback fencing unchanged;
unmeasured auxiliary GPU time stays null. Reason: adding a CPU completion wait
per face undermines amortized updates. Cost if wrong: more queued lifetimes and
subtle write/retirement ordering; validate shared writes, failure, resize and close
while queued. A queue receipt is not proof of physical completion or presentation.

Ruling: probe collections hold at most four probes and one candidate update, with
one capture or filter job per explicit advance, face sizes16..256,32MiB declared
old/candidate/capture/filter storage and16,777,216 integration samples per filtering
step (16Mi samples).
Latch capture position and content revision, ignoring ordinary main-camera/origin
changes; retain the old complete map until all faces and filters finish. Backend
attachments outside that declared storage are reported separately. Reason: bound
work and avoid half-updated reflections or perpetual restart during navigation.
Cost if wrong: update latency and rejected high-quality combinations; multiple
collections add aggregate work under the existing device budget and queue bounds.
Externally mutable GPU inputs are not claimed to be an immutable full snapshot.

Ruling: select one containing local probe per view/material by priority then
nearest object anchor; outside the volumes retains either existing global
environment model. Use double world coordinates and camera-relative native inputs.
Reason: deterministic bounded selection integrates local lighting without replacing
atmosphere/global fallback. Cost if wrong: object-anchor selection can change at
volume boundaries; the final implementation must state its actual parallax model
and cannot call a capture-point approximation parallax-correct.

Ruling: cap auxiliary capture leases at four per native device, with a documented
recoverable rejection and safe close/retry slot release. Reason: auxiliary views
retain their own scene/cache/target state alongside the main presenter. Cost if
wrong: applications needing more concurrent captures must schedule or close leases;
the cap must not weaken normal view limits or permit stale view identity reuse.

Ruling: add a small optional bounded resource retirement/ownership query or receipt,
and track every retained probe generation until reclamation is genuinely established.
Count shared BRDF storage once; bound metadata as well as bytes. Keep native cover
ownership intact and block/defer a candidate when retained generations plus new
work exceed32MiB. Couple final reclamation to targeted all-view alias invalidation;
registry lookup failure alone is not retirement proof because refs0 in-flight
entries and cached aliases may remain. Reason: old displayed covers must stay
renderable without hiding physical handle retention from logical budgets. Cost if
wrong: additional lifecycle API, queries and bookkeeping; inactive views may delay
updates until their covers change or close. Native staged/inactive/in-flight and
capacity-retry checks must verify the chosen mechanics.

Ruling: implement opt-in screen effects inside forward PBR using each actual
fragment's mapped normals, Task7 filtered roughness, metallic/F0 and energy terms,
with a separate view-local unmodified HDR opaque color/depth source capture.
Run any existing transmission/custom-input capture with effects afterward, then
main draws, preserving compatible seed reuse and group3. Reason: this supplies real
material inputs without a second approximate MRT material model. Cost if wrong:
extra opaque rendering and repeated ray work when seed reuse is unavailable;
current-cover/camera identity, attachment sampling hazards and pass accounting need
native validation. Misses preserve selected local/global fallback, while valid
screen hits must work even without an explicit environment.

Ruling: use deterministic stateless SSR/AO without jitter or temporal accumulation.
Fresh inputs from each actually executed cover establish temporal validity; test
cuts, resize, staged/failed publication and multiple views for stale lighting.
Reason: avoid introducing new accumulation noise and history ownership into this
optional forward path. Cost if wrong: no temporal smoothing and screen-sampling
aliasing limits; work repeats every enabled frame, and low sample budgets may need
higher settings. Document the absence of history rather than claim accumulation.

Ruling: screen effects default off, medium quality, with low/medium/high AO taps
8/12/16 and SSR steps16/32/64, full-resolution single-sample RGBA16F+Depth32F source,
and128MiB shared-device scratch budget including every live replacement generation.
Approve finite bounded world-unit AO/SSR parameters and deterministic one/four-tap
reflection filtering with roughness/screen-edge fade, exact settings in8cbrief.
Reason: explicit bounded cost and source-compatible main MSAA without MRT expansion.
Cost if wrong: an extra12bytes/pixel source, sample-edge limitations, high-resolution
replacement rejection and fixed per-fragment work; no silent downgrade hides these.
Shared scratch reuse is approved in principle, but retirement must follow completed
serials or an explicit bounded replacement boundary, preserving old state on failure.

Ruling: shared screen-lighting scratch replacement/retirement uses the existing
bounded native5second completion boundary for the latest queued submission, with
transactional candidate validation and all-view alias invalidation. Steady-size
reuse stays queue ordered without an extra fence. Reason: one current scratch pair
cannot hide retired generations still held by queued auxiliary captures. Cost if
wrong: occasional resize/disable/close latency or a bounded timeout; failures must
preserve old state and still attempt all cleanup. Nonowner close cannot invalidate
a newer owner, and byte reporting stays device-wide logical payload.

Ruling: benchmark auto, shadowsOff and sparse use adaptive device-default cloud
quality; named low, medium and high variants use their fixed presets. Record the
applied mode explicitly. Reason: the benchmark currently disables adaptation through
a default argument, so its auto label does not measure the ordinary app behavior.
Cost if wrong: comparison with older mislabeled runs is invalid; variant reports
must retain their settings and only matched workloads support performance claims.

Ruling: update integrated test expectations only where the named pass counters,
additive nullable profile schema and independently evaluated compensated PBR model
prove that the old expectation is stale. Preserve original tolerances and map/color
semantics, and distinguish cold energy-table generation from mesh draw counts.
Reason: full-suite tests still encode earlier diagnostic and single-scatter contracts.
Cost if wrong: changing an oracle could hide a regression, so each change needs its
recorded failing case, a demonstrated cause and a passing focused check; no renderer
behavior or tolerance change is authorized by this ruling.

Ruling: codec integration tests wait within their existing finite bound for both
quiet requests and the expected displayed tile identity, then retain their exact
identity, decoded-pixel and cleanup assertions. Reason: request completion can
precede the successful frame receipt that publishes visibleTileIds. Cost if wrong:
a loose wait could conceal excessive publication delay, so the existing bound
stays fixed and serial failing evidence must establish the original timing error;
no streamer behavior or concurrent selection tests are changed by this ruling.

Ruling: fix the narrow shared Flutter session-readiness regression exposed by
integrated tests, including valid borrowed remounts and any demonstrated input
activation consequence. Preserve the concurrent independent visible-host clock,
failed/initializing/closed guards and original failing test expectations. Reason:
a valid rendered session must remain usable after reattachment, and the combined
renderer cannot be qualified with repeatable lifecycle failures. Cost if wrong:
this touches a concurrent controller path beyond the original rendering changes,
so use a separate focused commit and lifecycle checks rather than reverting its
clock behavior or broadening the declarative/input architecture.

Ruling: the declarative model-click fixture requests unlitDiagnostic materials
from its limited fake backend and asserts SceneReady before sending the click.
Reason: the test exercises loaded-model event routing, but its backend cannot
render the default Standard material and correctly disables input after failure.
Cost if wrong: this fixture no longer covers Standard material loading, so retain
the independent native/default-Standard PBR coverage and do not change input or
capability enforcement to make an unsupported fake scene appear ready.

Ruling: preserve the updated canonical local documentation and commit reviewed
snapshots with source paths and content hashes under the owned qualification
directory. Do not force-add the ignored docs tree or import unrelated pending
content into the website. Reason: the repository deliberately separates local
sources from the website's committed publication snapshot. Cost if wrong: public
guides and fresh-clone docs do not gain these updates until the website import is
performed; state that limitation explicitly while keeping current package guidance
and the durable snapshots available for review.

Ruling: qualify each benchmark phase only after an accepted presentation at or
beyond its twelve-second duration, with no initial, interior or tail receipt gap
above one second at the existing hundred-millisecond polling interval. Require an
actually applied reversal and accepted camera motion on both sides, associated by
benchmark-private submitted frame and public camera revision records after normal
update hooks. Missing or unmatched receipt sources remain unknown. Report rates
over full measured wall duration, separately retaining presentation span and gaps.
Reason: early samples and a hypothetical motion curve do not establish sustained
navigation or a displayed reversal. Cost if wrong: a run that stalls over one second
and later recovers fails this liveness qualification; retain its measured diagnostics
and label zero observed receipts only when elapsed time is known, never as success.
